t.E579.agn: JECFA, which evaluated ferrous gluconate in 1987, included it in the provisional maximum tolerable daily intake (PMTDI) of 0.8 mg/kg body weight/day, expressed as iron (Fe) and applying to all sources of iron; in its 1975 evaluation it had recommended that the contribution of gluconic acid from all sources also be taken into account. In the EU it is authorised only in olives darkened by oxidation; EFSA's re-evaluation is ongoing.
t.E579.body: Enters the body as iron and gluconate.
t.E579.found.0: Black olives darkened by oxidation (in the EU max. 150 mg/kg, as iron)
t.E579.prod: Obtained by reacting calcium or barium gluconate with iron sulphate, or iron carbonate with gluconic acid.
t.E579.regx.0: Group PMTDI for iron 0.8 mg/kg body weight/day (as Fe).
t.E579.regx.1: Only in olives darkened by oxidation, max. 150 mg/kg (as Fe).
t.E579.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was issued in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E579.summary: The iron salt of gluconic acid. Stabilises the colour of black olives; a source of iron.
t.E579.what: An iron salt used to stabilise the black colour of olives darkened by oxidation (colour stabiliser).
